craft_claim: An invented creature, object, or law functions as a prop that prescribes specific imaginings; whimsical pleasure grows when the prop is internally consistent enough for the reader to imagine into it.

supporting_evidence.location: Mimesis as Make-Believe (Harvard UP, 1990), ch. 1 ('Props and Fictional Truths', pp. 38-43) and ch. 4
supporting_evidence.note: Walton treats representational works as props that, through principles of generation, prescribe imaginings and generate fictional truths; he regards engagement with them as continuous with children's games of make-believe.

Calvino literalizes a scientific premise (for example a once-closer Moon) and then reasons consistently inside the invented situation rather than treating it as a joke, so the premise operates as a prop the reader imagines through.
Ray compounds two ordinary animal names into a new creature that then behaves according to internally consistent absurd rules, so the neologism becomes a prop rather than a mere sound.

scope: Fiction, poetry, and essay that invent entities or worlds the reader is invited to imagine.
exceptions: Prop-oriented make-believe (Walton) uses an invented thing to communicate about the real world; that shading belongs nearer tone-philosophical or satirical-literature.
